summary: Baileys fork pulls libsignal from a mutable author-controlled GitHub branch
details: diezyxalisa-baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. Its package.json declares the `libsignal` dependency as `github:dzytzy/alya-baileys#latest` — an off-registry source pointing at a mutable branch on the same author's GitHub rather than a registry version range or a pinned commit SHA. On `npm install`, npm clones whatever that branch currently contains and runs any lifecycle scripts inside the cloned repository, with no version pin and no integrity check. Because the branch is mutable and under the publisher's sole control, the code that runs on an installer's machine can change at any time after this package was published. The dependency name also shadows the well-known upstream `libsignal` crypto library, so this entry replaces the expected implementation in the dependency tree. Separately, the fork wires an undocumented auto-follow of a hardcoded author-owned WhatsApp newsletter (120363411407993897@newsletter) into makeNewsletterSocket, which runs 10 seconds after socket startup using the installer's authenticated WhatsApp session unless the caller sets `autoFollowChannels:false`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
